deviations.what: firm_year is never de-duplicated (there is no unique() call), so repeated (firm_id, year) rows pass through the right joins on lines 25-27 and come out as repeated output rows, where the spec requires them collapsed to one.

notes: Every other rule checks out: filing_year dating, the cpc_seq == 0 filter, missing-class removal, base window fy+1 to fy+5, forward window fy-1 to fy-3, the anti-join for new classes, NA for an empty base, 0 for an empty forward set, and the column order. The default focal years 1987-2015 are not enforced in the function, which returns whatever years firm_year supplies; I read that as acceptable because firm_year defines the firm-years to produce.
